title: Analgesia with fentanyl and midazolam during interventional radiologic liver tumor ablation by catheter-based radiotherapy-safety and risk factors.
summary:
In order to make catheter-based radiotherapy (or in general: local therapy procedures) painless and stress-free for the patient, they are performed under concomitant analgesia. A combination of opiates and benzodiazepines (e.g., fentanyl and midazolam) usually allows interventional radiologists to provide effective analgesia and conserve anesthesia resources.
Data on safety and potential risk factors should be collected.
conditions: Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct

interventions.name: To retrospectively record the clinical findings of patients with liver tumors who underwent analgesia during interventional radiological tumor ablation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who have undergone local ablation therapy with catheter-based radiotherapy under analgesia for one or more liver tumors.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who have not undergone local ablation therapy with catheter-based radiotherapy under analgesia due to one or more liver tumors.
